record.paper_title: Some open questions on morphological operators and representations in the deep learning era: A personal vision
record.context_brief: MMBB networks and learned structuring-function bases
record.original_question: For nonlinear image transforms defined on complete lattices, can Matheron-Maragos-Banon-Barrera (MMBB) neural-network architectures effectively learn a minimal basis of structuring functions whose dilations, erosions, anti-dilations, and anti-erosions approximate any nonlinear image transform, and how should hierarchical deep-learning architectures be adapted for such MMBB networks?

evidence.quote: How effective MMBB networks would be to learn the minimal basis of structuring functions approximating any nonlinear image transform? How the idea of hierarchical architectures from deep learning can be used in the case of MMBB networks?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $(\mathcal{L}, \le)$ be a complete lattice (for instance, the lattice of grey-scale images $f:E\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ on a domain $E$, ordered pointwise). For a structuring function $g:E\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}$, define the flat/grey-scale operators on $\mathcal{L}$:
- dilation $\delta_g(f)(x)=\sup_{y\in E}\{f(x-y)+g(y)\}$,
- erosion $\varepsilon_g(f)(x)=\inf_{y\in E}\{f(x+y)-g(y)\}$,
- anti-dilation $\bar\delta_g(f)(x)=\inf_{y\in E}\{-f(x-y)-g(y)\}$,
- anti-erosion $\bar\varepsilon_g(f)(x)=\sup_{y\in E}\{-f(x+y)+g(y)\}$.

A classical representation theorem (Matheron–Maragos–Banon–Barrera, MMBB) asserts that every translation-invariant, increasing (or, more generally, suitably regular) nonlinear image operator $\Psi:\mathcal{L}\to\mathcal{L}$ can be expressed as a supremum of erosions (or, dually, an infimum of dilations) over a "basis" $\mathcal{B}(\Psi)$ of structuring functions, with analogous decompositions involving anti-dilations and anti-erosions for non-increasing operators. The minimal basis is the (unique, in the appropriate sense) smallest such family.

By an "MMBB neural network'' we mean a feed-forward parametric architecture whose layers compute finite combinations of the four primitive operations $\delta_{g_i}, \varepsilon_{g_i}, \bar\delta_{g_i}, \bar\varepsilon_{g_i}$ with learnable structuring functions $g_i$, together with lattice operations $\sup,\inf$.

Problem.
(a) Given a target nonlinear image operator $\Psi$ on $\mathcal{L}$, design an MMBB neural-network architecture and a training procedure that provably learn (from input–output samples $(f, \Psi f)$) a finite family of structuring functions $\{g_i\}$ approximating the minimal MMBB basis of $\Psi$ in the sense that the network's induced operator approximates $\Psi$ uniformly to within any prescribed $\varepsilon>0$. Quantify the sample and parameter complexity required.

(b) Formulate a notion of hierarchical (deep) MMBB architecture, i.e. a sensible way to stack MMBB layers so that intermediate representations correspond to learned bases of intermediate lattice operators, and determine whether such hierarchical MMBB networks can approximate operators that cannot be efficiently realized by a single MMBB layer of comparable size. In particular, identify a class of operators for which depth provably reduces the size of the learned basis.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a published resolution of the question of whether MMBB-style morphological neural networks can effectively learn a minimal basis of structuring functions approximating arbitrary nonlinear image transforms, nor a definitive theory of hierarchical/deep MMBB architectures. The question is posed as an open research direction and no source claims a complete solution; status is therefore taken to be open.
